items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a confident, energetic documentary narrator for a fast-paced animated martial-arts breakdown Short: part sports commentator, part history buff. PACE IS IMPORTANT: brisk, about 3.3 words per second; no slow drawn-out words and no long pauses (keep every pause under half a second). One steady voice and one steady energy from start to finish: crisp, punchy, a little amused, never shouting. A tiny beat before 'Time to cheat' and before the final question only. Do not change character or tone between lines.
lines: Two samurai. One duel. And we're about to freeze it.
Standoff. This is iaijutsu: drawing and cutting in one motion. It's mostly a counterattack, but it can also be a surprise strike.
The word is first tied to Iizasa Choisai, a master of the fourteen hundreds.
Steel meets steel, and the defender draws a second blade. This is Musashi's Niten Ichi-ryu: katana and wakizashi together.
Two heavens as one, to control distance and tempo.
Now he throws the sword. Yagyu Shinkage-ryu calls it Empi: swallow takes flight. Spearing an opponent with a thrown sword.
Time to cheat. A flying kick into a spinning jump cut. Pure cinema. We couldn't find it in any documented school.
Disarmed? Yagyu Shinkage-ryu has an answer: Muto. Bare hands against a sword.
Five moves. Four are real. Which one would you pick?
